summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built bare-metal embedded firmware development in C and FreeRTOS across ARM Cortex-M microcontroller architectures, with register-level GPIO/ADC/I2C peripheral drivers and interrupt-driven UART command handling. Shipped embedded software integrating I2C/UART/Ethernet-connected sensor buses, servo control, and real-time task coordination across STM32, Arduino, and NVIDIA Jetson microcontrollers.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed embedded firmware for a wearable gesture-recognition glove, integrating ADXL345 accelerometers over I2C with a Raspberry Pi microcontroller and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through firmware-level calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C serial protocols with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Used Git/GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative technical documentation in a laboratory research environment.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware for real-time temperature monitoring using bare-metal embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on ARM Cortex-M architecture; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on an Arduino microcontroller in C++; drove five servos with range-gated I2C contact detection via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer.
Deployed the Jetson-side embedded control bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart, non-root isolation, environment-based config) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device communication.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to an ARM Cortex-M STM32 microcontroller over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.
Ran FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on the microcontroller firmware; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C and OLED distance visualization.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
